extracted.intended_audience: scholars in the humanities and social sciences; applicants and members interested in ACLS programs, fellowships, and history
extracted.subtask_description: A descriptive overview of the American Council of Learned Societies (ACLS), its mission, history, fellowship and grant programs, publication initiatives (Humanities E-Book), awards, and international exchange activities. Useful for scholars seeking background on ACLS funding, selection processes, and programmatic priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigorous peer review for ACLS awards
rubrics_metrics.description: All ACLS awards are made through rigorous peer review by specially appointed committees of scholars from throughout the United States, and, in some programs, abroad.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection is committee-based and peer-reviewed; awards rely on expert panels specially appointed by ACLS, indicating disciplinary peer evaluation as the standard selection mechanism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellowship eligibility across career stages and disciplines
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellowship competitions provide a range of opportunities for scholars in the humanities and related social sciences at all career stages, from graduate students to distinguished professors to independent scholars, working with a number of disciplines and methodologies in the U.S. and abroad.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs are intended to be inclusive of career stage and methodological diversity; applicants may include graduate students, early-career researchers, senior scholars, and independent researchers across multiple disciplines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for digital innovation in humanistic research
rubrics_metrics.description: ACLS developed grant and fellowship programs to encourage computer use in humanistic research and continues this work in programs such as the Digital Innovation Fellowships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACLS explicitly promotes projects that apply new technologies to humanities research; programmatic support and fellowships target digital humanities, computational methods, and exploration of new research technologies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee-based development of promising fields and area studies
rubrics_metrics.description: ACLS has organized committees to research promising fields of study and to organize expertise around cultural regions (e.g., Far Eastern, Slavic, African, Asian, Latin American, Near and Middle Eastern studies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACLS convenes expert committees to identify, research, and promote emerging or strategically important subfields and area studies; program priorities can be set by committee findings and perceived practical need.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for scholarly publication and dissemination
rubrics_metrics.description: ACLS has an interest in the problems of scholarly publication and has conducted surveys of publication needs, established a publication service to advise scholars on communicating research, and aided scholars with subsidies and publication assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACLS provides services and subsidies to improve scholarly communication; initiatives include investigations (e.g., National Enquiry into the Production and Dissemination of Scholarly Knowledge), an Office of Scholarly Communication and Technology, and practical advice to authors and presses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humanities E-Book (HEB) selection and quality standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The Humanities E-Book collection was launched with titles that had been reviewed and recommended by historians and scholarly societies and were often award-winning books; HEB's mission expanded to include all humanities disciplines and to provide high-quality electronically accessible titles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inclusion in HEB emphasizes works vetted by historians and societies, recognized for quality (often award-winning), and covering humanities disciplines broadly. Management and access are institutional (subscription) and/or administered by partner institutions (e.g., University of Michigan).

rubrics_metrics.name: Graves Awards criterion: outstanding teaching in early career
rubrics_metrics.description: The Graves Awards in the Humanities is a biannual award granted to young scholars in the first decade of their careers to 'encourage and reward outstanding accomplishment in actual teaching in the humanities.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility is limited to early-career scholars (within ten years), and the evaluative focus is on demonstrated excellence in undergraduate/actual teaching, not solely research output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awards recognizing exemplary advocacy for arts and sciences
rubrics_metrics.description: The Arts & Sciences Advocacy Award (as bestowed on ACLS) is given to an individual or organization demonstrating exemplary advocacy for the arts and sciences, flowing from a deep commitment to the intrinsic worth of liberal arts education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This type of award stresses public advocacy and sustained commitment to the value of liberal arts education rather than strictly scholarly metrics; selection favors demonstrable advocacy impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programmatic support for international scholarly exchange
rubrics_metrics.description: ACLS participates in and helps administer international exchange and capacity-building programs (e.g., involvement with the Fulbright-related Council for International Exchange of Scholars, American Studies Program abroad, ACLS Center for Educational Exchange with Vietnam, Committee on Scholarly Communication with China, programs in former USSR and Africa).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACLS evaluates and funds programs that promote international scholarly exchange, support overseas scholars, and build institutional links; priority is given to initiatives that foster cross-national collaboration and capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advocacy and public representation of humanities scholarship
rubrics_metrics.description: By bringing scholars together as scholars rather than as specialists, the ACLS advocates for the humanities in public forums and policy arenas and plays a role in establishing and reauthorizing national humanities institutions (e.g., role in establishing and reauthorizing the National Endowment for the Humanities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACLS's evaluative stance includes public advocacy and policy engagement as part of its mission; activities that strengthen the public presence and policy influence of humanities scholarship are central programmatic values.
